meta: Jusepe de Ribera's 1632 painting of Ixion, bound in chains and tortured by Zeus, one of a series of four condemned figures.
about: Chains bind a muscular nude man whose body twists and shortens sharply against a dark ground. He is Ixion, whom Zeus punished with eternal torture in Greek myth. Jusepe de Ribera signed and dated the painting in 1632. It was one of a series of four paintings of the condemned, the others showing Sisyphus and Tantalus. The Prado holds Ixion and the Tityos. Sisyphus and Tantalus are lost.

meta: Murillo's Aranjuez Immaculate Conception, painted around 1675 and named after the palace chapel where it was first recorded.
about: A woman in a white robe and blue mantle rises on clouds, her hands crossed over her chest and her eyes lifted. Putti gather at the base of the canvas. Bartolomé Esteban Murillo painted her around 1675. The picture takes its name from the palace at Aranjuez, where it first turns up in written records in 1818. It hung in the royal chapel of San Antonio. By 1827 it was in the queen's quarters of the same palace. It is now in the Prado.

meta: Peter Paul Rubens's The Origin of the Milky Way, painted for Philip IV's hunting lodge, shows Hera spilling her milk across the sky.
about: Milk arcs across a dark, star-filled sky from the breast of a nude goddess beside a chariot drawn by peacocks. Peter Paul Rubens painted this scene of Hera, known to the Romans as Juno, spilling her milk over the infant Heracles. Zeus looks on, identifiable by his eagle. Hera's face is modelled on Rubens's wife, Hélène Fourment. Philip IV of Spain commissioned it for the Torre de la Parada, his hunting lodge near Madrid, as one of 112 paintings based on Ovid. It is now in the Prado.

meta: David Teniers the Younger's 1665 peasant kermis: dancing outside an inn, a drunk man among the pigs and a banner in the window.
about: Outside an inn, peasants dance to a bagpiper while large parties eat and drink at long tables on either side. A drunk man has fallen among the pigs, and his wife is hauling him back to his feet. At left a maid draws water from a well. A banner showing a knight with a bow and arrows hangs from the inn window. David Teniers the Younger signed the picture on a block of stone at lower right. The city of Amsterdam lent it to the Rijksmuseum from the A. van der Hoop bequest.

meta: Johan Diderik Cornelis Veltens's 1865 drawing of the surroundings of the Polderhuis, kept in the Atlas Van Eck.
about: A canal runs between wooden houses, past a tall chimney and a sluice or mill with paddle wheels on the right. Small rowing boats and figures move along the water, and a woman with laundry stands on the bank beside a dog. Johan Diderik Cornelis Veltens drew the scene in pencil, pen and brush in grey. It belongs to the Atlas Van Eck, where the drawings are sorted by district number, and this one is filed under 26. The Koninklijk Oudheidkundig Genootschap lends it to the Rijksmuseum.

meta: Albrecht Dürer's 1510 woodcut of Veronica holding the sweat cloth with the face of Christ, from the Small Passion series.
about: Veronica holds up the sweat cloth bearing the face of Christ, with Saint Peter and Saint Paul standing on either side. Peter has his keys and Paul his sword. Albrecht Dürer made this woodcut in 1510. It belongs to the Small Passion, a series of a title print and 36 scenes from the Bible, most of them from the story of Christ's suffering. The face on the cloth wears a crown of thorns.

meta: Gerbrand van den Eeckhout's 1663 watercolour view of Rhenen and the Rhine, bought by the Rijksmuseum in 1894.
about: A broad river landscape opens out beneath the church tower of Rhenen, which rises above the houses of a town on a low ridge. Small sailing boats sit on the water at left. Gerbrand van den Eeckhout drew it in 1663 in watercolour over black chalk and graphite. The drawing was sold at an Amsterdam sale in 1893, and the next year the Rijksmuseum bought it from the dealer H.J. Valk for 22 guilders 95.

meta: Gerbrand van den Eeckhout's 1667 pen drawing of guild officers around a table, sold in 1847 as a sketch for a painting.
about: Men in wide-brimmed hats and lace collars gather around a table, some seated and one standing behind them. Gerbrand van den Eeckhout drew them in 1667 with pen and brown ink in loose, quick strokes. An 1847 sale catalogue described the sheet as a sketch for a painting that had belonged to the guild of gaugers in Amsterdam. The Rijksmuseum bought it with support from the Vereniging Rembrandt.

meta: Gerbrand van den Eeckhout's 1653 chalk drawing of a boy asleep in a chair, with a collecting history back to 1800.
about: A boy in a wide-brimmed hat and buttoned jacket sleeps slumped sideways in a wooden chair. Gerbrand van den Eeckhout drew him in black chalk with grey wash. The sheet belonged to the collector Cornelis Ploos van Amstel, whose sale in 1800 listed it as a young man asleep on a chair. It went in a lot with two other drawings for 5 guilders 50. In 1871 it was sold again in Rotterdam from the collection of Dirk Vis Blokhuyzen and bought for 1 guilder by Baron Willem van Reede van Oudtshoorn.

meta: Samuel Bottschild's 1693 etching of Nox, Night, from a series of 48 prints mostly designed for ceilings.
about: A winged woman holds a crescent moon and scatters stars, while a figure sleeps beside her at lower right. The word Nox is inscribed at the foot of the circle. Samuel Bottschild etched it for a series published in 1693, Opera Varia Historica, Poetica & Iconologica. The series has 48 prints and covers almost everything the artist made. Most of them are designs for ceilings.

meta: Christoffel van Sichem the Younger's 1629 woodcut of the Tree of Jesse, first used in the book Der Zielen Lust-hof.
about: Jesse lies at the bottom with his elbow on a stone, and a tree grows from his body. The ancestors of Christ sit on its branches, and the Virgin with the Child crowns the top. Christoffel van Sichem the Younger made the woodcut, which came from the publisher P.J. Paets in Amsterdam. It was first used in the book Der Zielen Lust-hof, printed in Leuven for Paets in 1629. The museum's copy is mounted on an album sheet.

meta: Romeyn de Hooghe's 1690 bird's-eye print of Het Loo Palace, part of a much larger view with thirteen smaller scenes around it.
about: A bird's-eye view takes in a palace and its formal gardens, with geometric parterres, rows of clipped trees and fountains. Carriages and horsemen move through the grounds. Romeyn de Hooghe made the print in 1690, but it is only part of a bigger work. The museum describes it as half of a view of Het Loo, spread over four sheets or possibly two. The whole print put the palace in the middle, with thirteen views of its buildings and park around it and a profile of the palace at the bottom.

meta: Charles Emile Jacque's 1864 etching of a path, a cow and a seated woman with a child, from a series of 25 rural scenes.
about: A dirt path winds through open ground between a tall poplar and a broad leafy tree. In the foreground a woman sits beside a small child holding a stick, and a cow grazes nearby. Charles Emile Jacque etched it in 1864. It comes from an untitled series of 25 prints with rural and pastoral subjects, which was published that year.

meta: Jan Brandes's 1778 watercolour of a Cape chestnut branch in flower, drawn at the Constantia estate near the Cape of Good Hope.
about: A branch of broad green leaves and pink star-shaped flowers fills the sheet, with a small sketch below it. Jan Brandes drew it on 23 October 1778 at Constantia, an estate at the Cape of Good Hope. He had asked its owner, Mr Leseur, to have a twig cut so that he could take a look. The tree was only just beginning to flower and leaf. Brandes wrote that the fruit would be like a cherry with a small seed, which chickens and turkeys ate as soon as it fell. Nobody knew the name. The drawing comes from the first volume of his sketchbook.

meta: John Raphael Smith's 1780 mezzotint The Fruit-Barrow, after H. Walton, a group portrait of uncertain identity.
about: A fruit seller stands at a barrow beside a brick wall with ivy, attended by a woman in a long gown and feathered hat and several children. The mezzotint is titled The Fruit-Barrow. It was painted by H. Walton and engraved by John Raphael Smith around 1780. Nobody is sure who the family is. The Rijksmuseum suggests it may be a Mrs Carr, or else members of the family of Henry Walton.

meta: Daniël Bruyninx's signed 1761 miniature portrait of a man in a blue coat, set in a silver case.
about: A man with powdered grey hair wears a blue coat with gold embroidered trim over a red waistcoat and a black neckcloth. The portrait is a small oval miniature set in an open silver case lined with green velvet. Daniël Bruyninx signed and dated it 1761. In 1918 a dealer named Van Waegeningh in The Hague sold it for 125 guilders to Adolph Staring van de Wildenborch of Deventer. His widow later gave it to the museum, with other objects, in 1981.

meta: Jan van Noordt's 1664 portrait of the Amsterdam merchant Dionijs Wijnands, shown to the knees beside a table with his hat and gloves.
about: A man stands at a table, shown to the knees, with his hat and gloves lying on the tabletop. He wears black with a broad white collar and gold-trimmed cuffs, and an arched opening at the right looks out on a stormy sky. Jan van Noordt signed the portrait in 1664. The sitter is Dionijs Wijnands, an Amsterdam merchant who lived from 1628 to 1673. He was the son of Hendrick Wijnands and Aeltje Denijs. The portrait reached the Rijksmuseum in the bequest of Jonkheer J.S.H. van de Poll.

meta: Joseph Boze's signed miniature portrait of Gerrit Jan van Houten, later burgomaster of Amersfoort, painted around 1790.
about: A smiling man with curly dark hair wears a dark high-collared coat and a white frilled cravat against a pale grey-blue ground. Joseph Boze painted this oval miniature around 1790 and signed it. The sitter is Gerrit Jan van Houten, who became burgomaster of Amersfoort. It has a pendant in the same museum. Lieutenant-Colonel Marius Cornelis van Houten gave it to the Rijksmuseum in 1933 but kept the use of it for life. It passed to the museum in 1953.

meta: Abraham van Strij's chalk and brush drawing of a man in a fur hat seen in profile, given to the Rijksmuseum in 1939.
about: A man in profile faces right in a large fur hat with feathered plumes, a fur-trimmed coat and a white cravat. Abraham van Strij drew the head in brush in brown and red with black and white chalk on brown paper. He signed it at upper right. In 1939 the dealer J.H.J. Mellaart of Scheveningen gave it to the museum together with 30 other drawings.

meta: Anton Weiss's 1836 lithograph of a flowering branch, one sheet from a cover holding 41 prints of flowers and fruit.
about: Soft grey shading models a flowering branch, with clusters of open blossoms, buds and serrated leaves along a textured stem. Anton Weiss made the lithograph in 1836. The sheet belongs to a cover that holds a series of 41 lithographs of flowers and fruit. It carries a printed notice of registration, the word Gedeponeerd.

meta: Romeyn de Hooghe's 1667 engraving of the Peace of Breda, with the oath-taking in the centre and six smaller scenes around it.
about: Delegates gather around a table in a crowded hall to swear to a peace treaty, with six smaller scenes arranged around the central one. Romeyn de Hooghe made this multi-panel engraving of the Peace of Breda, signed on 31 July 1667, which ended the Second Anglo-Dutch War. The scenes above and below show the English ambassadors arriving and leaving. The sides show the proclamation of the peace and the celebrations. Keys marked A to I under the central scene explain the details.

meta: Georg Leopold Hertel's 1761 etching of a bearded old man in a fur cap, a mirror-image copy after Rembrandt.
about: A bearded old man in a high fur cap and dark cloak turns his wrinkled face to one side, his eyes downcast. Georg Leopold Hertel made this etching in 1761. It copies Rembrandt's print of the same title, but in mirror image. Rembrandt's own etching shows the old man facing the other way.

meta: Johann Jakob Schübler's engraved design for organ cases, the first of six prints from his book of organ casings and wall pulpits.
about: Two organ cases stand side by side, split down the middle, with Baroque scrollwork, carved finials and rows of pipes. Keyboards, open sheet music and pedal boards show at the base. Johann Jakob Schübler engraved the design in 1699. It is the first of six prints from his book Neu Faconirte Orgel-verkleidungen und unterschiedliche Wand Cantzeln, published in Nuremberg by Weigel before 1726.

meta: Giovanni Battista Piranesi's 1748 etching of the Piazza del Popolo in Rome, from his Vedute di Roma series.
about: A tall Egyptian obelisk stands in the middle of the Piazza del Popolo in Rome, with two domed churches, Santa Maria in Montesanto and Santa Maria dei Miracoli, flanking the open square. Carriages and walkers cross the foreground among scattered fragments of architecture. Giovanni Battista Piranesi made the etching in 1748 as part of Vedute di Roma. He kept working on that series of 135 plates until his death in 1778, and his son Francesco later added two more.

meta: Tobias Conrad Lotter's 1767 hand-coloured family tree of the House of Orange-Nassau, ending with William V and Wilhelmina of Prussia.
about: A family tree of the House of Orange-Nassau climbs toward Prince William V and his wife Wilhelmina of Prussia, whose portraits are carried by putti at the top. The extinct Nassau-Dillenburg line runs up the left and ends with Stadtholder-King William III. On the right is the Frisian branch, Nassau-Dietz, with Johan Willem Friso and William IV. A text framed by laurel leaves in the centre is about the house itself. Tobias Conrad Lotter made the sheet in 1767 as an etching and engraving coloured by hand.

meta: An extraordinary issue of the Haagsche Courant from 1795, reporting a public festival for the alliance between France and the Batavian Republic.
about: A newspaper page reports a public festival held for the alliance between the French and Batavian Republics. The festival took place in The Hague on 16 May 1795. This extraordinary issue of the Haagsche Courant followed on 8 June. The text runs in four columns, and a stylised liberty tree stands in the middle. Borders and vignettes carry the figures of Prudence, Batavian Liberty and Strength. The vignettes are woodcuts.

meta: Johannes Wierix's 1579 engraving of Antiochus Epiphanes looting the Temple of Jerusalem, with a Latin caption citing 1 Maccabees.
about: Soldiers on horseback and on foot loot a temple, carrying off a candelabrum and gold vessels while figures lie fallen in the street. The scene is Antiochus Epiphanes in Jerusalem. The Rijksmuseum sums up the story this way: after his victory over Egypt he marched on the city with a large army, emptied the temple and killed many of its people. A Latin line beneath points to the Bible text 1 Maccabees 1:22. Johannes Wierix engraved it in 1579.

meta: Johannes Hubertus Reygers's 1817 print of a medal struck for the new harbour of Middelburg.
about: Two medal designs sit side by side on one sheet. The left shows sailing ships at a harbour quay under an inscription naming the new harbour of Middelburg, while the other design shows a seated woman. The medal was struck to mark the opening of that harbour on 9 August 1817. A note on the back records it as number 650 among the medals at the book auction of Professor J.W. te Water in October 1823.

meta: Daniël Bruyninx's 1758 miniature of a lady with a fan, painted inside the lid of a mother-of-pearl box.
about: A woman in a lace cap and blue dress with white ruffled trim sits holding an open fan, with the back of a green upholstered chair behind her. Daniël Bruyninx signed and dated the miniature 1758. It forms the inside of the lid of a small box of mother-of-pearl and gilt silver. The box is decorated with rocaille ornament and a lute-playing muse with a lion and a bird. The Rijksmuseum bought it from the dealer A. Aardewerk in The Hague in 1991 for 19,080 guilders.

meta: Jan van de Velde the Younger's 1603 engraving of two pilgrims beside a pond, the third print in a series of six.
about: Two pilgrims in cloaks and wide-brimmed hats stand on a grassy bank at the edge of a pond. One holds a staff and turns toward the viewer, while the other is seen from behind. Far off, two small figures carry baskets on their backs, and dense trees fill the right side of the scene. Jan van de Velde the Younger engraved it in 1603. Third of six.

meta: Paulus Lauters's 1831 lithograph of King Leopold I riding into Brussels through the decorated Porte d'Anvers.
about: A procession passes beneath a white triumphal arch topped with flags, with mounted riders and rows of soldiers lining the street. Spectators fill the balconies and pavement on the right. The scene is the ceremonial arrival of King Leopold I at the Koningsplein in Brussels on 21 July 1831. The king rides in with his entourage through the Porte d'Anvers, which was decorated for the day and had earlier been called the Willemspoort. A companion print exists.

meta: Jan de Lange's 1822 coloured woodcut sheet with six scenes from Tom Thumb above and six from Puss in Boots below.
about: Twelve hand-coloured woodcut panels share one sheet, each with a Dutch caption beneath it. The top six tell the fairy tale of Tom Thumb, and the bottom six tell that of Puss in Boots. Jan de Lange made the sheet in 1822 with colours in blue, yellow and brown. It is numbered 5 at upper right. The Tom Thumb scenes begin in a woodcutter's household and show children hiding.

meta: Dirk Noothoven van Goor's 1850 sheet of four street vendors, number 111 of the Prenten-Magazijn voor de Jeugd.
about: Four small scenes of street trades in a Dutch town share this sheet. They show a fruit seller, an umbrella seller, a seller of sour pickled goods and a milkmaid. Each has a title above and an eight-line verse beneath. The sheet is number 111 of the Prenten-Magazijn voor de Jeugd, a print magazine for young people, and Dirk Noothoven van Goor made the wood engraving in 1850. Colours in blue, yellow and red were added.

meta: Jan Rinke's 1910 cartoon of the Amsterdam councillor L. Simons as a swan on the canal, issued with De Nieuwe Amsterdammer.
about: A man's head with a pointed nose and glasses sits on the body of a swan floating in a canal. Behind it a woman in a crown and a sash with the Amsterdam crosses stands with one hand raised, plainly dismayed. She is the city maiden of Amsterdam. Jan Rinke aimed the cartoon at the councillor L. Simons. A four-line verse by Potgieter runs beneath. It appeared as a supplement to De Nieuwe Amsterdammer on 11 November 1910.

meta: Gerrit Willem Dijsselhof's 1876 pencil drawing of a rock face, given to the Rijksmuseum by his daughter in 1969.
about: A steep rock face rises in pencil, with jagged outcrops and loose boulders along the lower edge. Loose hatching and smudged shading suggest rough stone and the air around it. Gerrit Willem Dijsselhof drew it in 1876. The drawing stayed in his family. His daughter, Johanna Dijsselhof of Deventer, gave it to the Rijksmuseum with other objects in 1969.

meta: Willem Wenckebach's 1892 cover design for Thérèse Hoven's In sarong en kabaai, with four houses in a circle of palms.
about: Within a circle stand four houses in a landscape of the Dutch East Indies. Palm trees surround the circle, and a draped sarong hangs unfolded around it. Willem Wenckebach drew this as a cover design for Thérèse Hoven's book In sarong en kabaai, which covers the years 1892 to 1894. He used pen in India ink and gold paint over pencil, on card. Gold lettering gives the title.

meta: Adolf van der Laan's etched proof showing the inner courtyard of the Huiszittenweduwenhof, also called the Kartuizerhof, in Amsterdam.
about: Two tall trees stand before a central building with a pedimented entrance, flanked by brick wings. This is the inner courtyard of the Huiszittenweduwenhof in Amsterdam, also called the Kartuizerhof. It was built on the site of the former Carthusian monastery. The sheet is a proof cut from the right-hand plate of a larger print by Adolf van der Laan. That print showed ground plans of two charitable buildings, framed by allegories, coats of arms and views of their parts. A handwritten title sits below.

meta: Anna Alma Tadema's 1880 drawing of a goose in a blue medallion, one of the vignette designs in an album for framing photographs.
about: A goose with an orange beak and orange legs wades among reeds inside a blue circular medallion. A grey border of interlocking scalloped shapes surrounds it. Anna Alma Tadema painted it in 1880. The drawing belongs to an album of vignette designs. They were made to frame photographs that would be pasted in.

meta: Lilly Martin Spencer's 1860 We Both Must Fade shows Mrs. Fithian at her mirror in lace, pearls and a blue gown.
about: Mrs. Fithian stands before a mirror, admiring the tokens that others have given in praise of her beauty. She wears lace and pearls and a blue satin gown with a lace overlay, and the gown has just been taken from its box. In her hand is a pink rose, and she looks down. A jewelry box, a pearl necklace and a vase of flowers sit on the table beside her. Scattered petals lie on the floor. Lilly Martin Spencer painted the scene in 1860.

meta: Marsden Hartley's Popocatepetl, Spirited Morning, a snow-capped volcano above dark violet slopes, inspired by Mexico.
about: A white snowy summit rises above a band of dark violet slopes, and heavy rounded clouds fill the lower part of the canvas. The mountain is Popocatépetl, near Mexico City. The Smithsonian American Art Museum says that Marsden Hartley was entranced by the two snow-capped volcanoes around the city, Popocatépetl and Ixtaccihuatl, during a visit in 1932.

meta: Jan Bernardus Ulrich's 1816 woodcut sheet of 48 small scenes with verses, number 17 in a printed series for children.
about: A grid of 48 small woodcut scenes fills the sheet, among them a lion, a boy with a hoop and a ship on the water. Under each is a two-line verse. Jan Bernardus Ulrich's sheet dates from 1816 and is coloured in yellow, blue and orange. It is numbered 17 at lower right. The heading across the top invites the viewer to spend time with joy and learning.

meta: Caterino Doino's engraved double portrait of Alfonso II and Cesare d'Este, made for a book on the d'Este princes printed at Ferrara in 1641.
about: Two bearded men in ruff collars stand side by side, each holding a slender staff. The caption names them as Alfonso II, Duke of Ferrara, and Cesare, Duke of Modena. Caterino Doino engraved the portrait for a book by Antonio Cariola on the princes of Este, the lords of Ferrara, which Francesco Suzzi printed in Ferrara in 1641. The Rijksmuseum has the print in an album. Two dukes.

meta: Cornelis Troost's drawing of the shepherd couple Kloris and Roosje dancing in the country while a shepherd plays the flute.
about: Kloris and Roosje dance together in front of a thatched farmhouse. In the lower right corner a shepherd sits under a large tree and plays a flute. Far off on the horizon, windmills and towers rise above the flat land, and the Rijksmuseum thinks they may belong to Amsterdam. Cornelis Troost drew the scene in pen and grey wash. The Koninklijk Oudheidkundig Genootschap lends it to the museum.
